decisions.reason: The original open-set intersection clause is vacuous and does not impose face-to-face closure intersections. Replaced it by an explicit condition on closures. Also made the declared fixed polygon-shape parameters explicit: scaled Lipschitz graph count, radius and constants, and mean-zero Poincaré constants; the notch family in the Step-4 digest shows that pointwise cones alone cannot give uniform Euclidean trace constants. This qualification retains all fixed polygonal models with their actual shape constants and the intended uniform bounded-shape estimates.

The matrix is the local stiffness matrix of the symmetric bilinear form a_i(v,w)=rho_i sum_K integral grad(v) dot grad(w), inherited through the Schur definition and scalar model. Thus K_i is symmetric, both cross terms vanish when its interior row on H_i g is zero, and the positive interior quadratic term proves the unique minimum even for a floating block or empty interior.

The PE26 corner branch inherits rho_i>0 from the scalar model through both its primal-space and Schur-definition dependencies. Hence rho_i+rho_j>0, the two weights sum to one and preserve conforming values. The inverse in the BDDC formula is explicitly restricted to a positive definite partial Schur operator. No edit is needed.

The original S_i was Dirichlet-restricted, so arbitrary nonzero outer-boundary data were outside its domain. Preserved the full arbitrary-trace estimate by defining the floating Schur matrix S_i^fl, proving its fixed-trace minimum by the symmetric block identity, and identifying its energy with S_i precisely for admissible zero-Dirichlet traces. The chart proof now uses the explicit scaled shape parameters, and the boundary-mean inequality works even when the boundary has multiple components; the averaging interpolant preserves every P1 trace and is H1 stable by bounded patch overlap.

The original generic construction allowed no primal constraints on a floating subdomain, leaving a nonzero constant trace in the kernel of tilde S while using its inverse. Added the explicit symmetric-positive-definite admissibility requirement; the all-corners-primal theorem is a sufficient PE26 branch, not a claim about arbitrary constraints. The right inverse remains well defined by the direct-sum projection, BB_D^T=I and B_D^TB=I-RE_0. The inherited Euclidean identification of Lambda with its dual is now explicit for coordinate formulas.

The displayed operators themselves are well typed, but the proof incorrectly labels X and Y with U_2 rather than its dual. Corrected X:U_2'→U_1 and Y:U_1→U_2', and located eigenvectors in those spaces. The given complementary identities give G_1-I=-XY and G_2-I=-YX; the scaled X map inverts Y on every nonunit eigenspace. In dual bases each product is similar to an SPD matrix, so eigenspace multiplicity is algebraic multiplicity. This is a nonfatal annotation error; the unchanged statement is true.

F3 was an overbroad quotation of an all-subdomain-vertices-primal sufficient criterion, while only the shared endpoints are primal here. This is nonfatal because the preceding zero-top-side anchoring already kills the constant kernel on each local square, independently of primal choice. Corrected the quotation and made that direct positive-definiteness proof explicit: a zero partial energy has two zero local energies, hence two constants, both zero by the top side. Recomputed triangle gradients and the four-cycle quadratic form; all shared nodes are endpoints and there are no interior nodes, so exact condensation applies.

A generic dense cost model does not imply the PE26 spectral bound. Added all hypotheses of the cited two-dimensional theorem to the example and Given, with fixed geometric constants and H/h, SPD local dual/coarse blocks, and nonzero preconditioned spaces. Replaced the incompatible one-primal-variable-per-subdomain premise by the actual assumption n_c proportional to N, allowing all corners primal. Standard dense Cholesky gives local O(Nm^3) work, ideal O(m^3) local time, and coarse O(N^3) work/O(N^2) storage while the theorem gives an N-independent condition bound.
